overview: Sukhothai, which broke from Khmer rule about 1238, is remembered as the first Thai kingdom. Its inscription of Ram Khamhaeng describes a father-king, its sculptors made the walking Buddha, and its script became the Thai alphabet.

items.text: The Ram Khamhaeng inscription, dated 1283, says the king devised the Thai script from Khmer models; some scholars date the stone itself to the fifteenth century.
The walking Buddha, a figure in motion cast in bronze, is Sukhothai's own creation.
Lotus-bud chedis at Wat Mahathat and Sri Lankan-style bell stupas; glazed Sawankhalok stoneware was exported across the region.
Theravada Buddhism of the Sri Lankan school, brought by monks from Nakhon Si Thammarat, became the state religion.
The inscription describes a king who hears any subject's grievance when they ring the bell at the palace gate.
The Historic Town of Sukhothai and Associated Historic Towns were listed by UNESCO.
The Thai alphabet descends from the Sukhothai script.

fall.text: Ayutthaya reduced Sukhothai to a vassal in 1378 and, when its royal line ended in 1438, made it a province.

sources.title: UNESCO, Historic Town of Sukhothai and Associated Historic Towns
